rationale: The original negative Unicode and ASCII word-boundary assertions remain invalid: they conflate not matching the empty haystack with inability to match an empty substring in context. Passing on broken production and failing on fixed production is discrimination in the wrong direction, not a basis for correct expectations. Reaffirmed the prior independent issue 859 semantic-basis review, complete source/test identities, generated lock, six one-test Cargo and frozen-artifact replay captures, and separate regex::Regex matcher witness. This packaging review verified that all seven retained source/test/matcher payloads and their reconstructed copies are byte-identical to the previously accepted assets; only their portable data locators now end in .rs.txt. Four matcher program locators and their enclosing key/pairing descriptors were propagated without altering historical commands, inventories, executable identities, outputs or verdicts. Reconstructed parent-archive-plus-lock/source/test identities match all six 249-entry before/after native inventories. The frozen raw packet b910ec9fafcdca9e1783218df877f8900313362a7741c51716d1c950a9045a0b and native receipt 8dca1d09ece7506e6f32302e310c55f0efc0eb6dcacb105e5cbdff88d74fe6b8 are unchanged. Executable byte rehashes belong to the earlier review and retained dated measurements; this packaging review performed no new native execution or executable rehash. External executable custody remains NOT_REVERIFIED by the fixture consumer. Weak remains only a removal control. Failing whole-test runs stop at the first Unicode assertion; later ASCII assertion execution is not claimed for those runs. This accepts exactly the rebound semantic declaration and historical capture subject, not the validator implementation, static analysis, calibration/opportunity credit or release.
